system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41, ivy.chen's PowerShell command archived the Clients directory from \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared into C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip, and Sysmon recorded creation of that archive.
ivy.chen then launched Edge to quickshare-drop.net, a service not listed among the organization's approved services in the provided inventory.

The proxy recorded a 51,000,000-byte client-to-server transfer through a CONNECT tunnel to quickshare-drop.net, with only 8,800 bytes in the server-to-client direction; Zeek independently recorded approximately 51 MB sent over the corresponding proxy connection.

The close sequence—archiving client materials, opening an unapproved file-sharing destination, and sending about 51 MB—strongly supports an inference of unauthorized data exfiltration from WS-ICHEN-01.
A separate executable named KB5034441_update.exe ran from the user's Temp directory with a quiet argument; the available records do not connect it to the outbound transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy and Zeek records establish tunnel byte counts, but the supplied records do not expose the TLS-encrypted request contents or identify the uploaded file.
The archive creation record establishes that c.zip was created, but the supplied records do not show its size, contents, or a direct link between that archive and the tunnel transfer.
The supplied records do not establish whether ivy.chen had authorization for this transfer or identify who controlled quickshare-drop.net.
claims_not_established: That c.zip, specifically, was the file uploaded; the timing and volume are suggestive but do not prove the payload's identity.
What client data, if any, was included in the archive or transferred.
Whether the transfer was authorized by the organization or user.
Whether KB5034441_update.exe was malicious or related to the transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and examine c.zip, including its hash, size, contents, and creation/access metadata.
Obtain endpoint file-access and browser upload telemetry, and any available TLS inspection or destination-side upload records, to identify the transferred payload.
Verify whether the transfer was authorized and investigate the ownership and reputation of quickshare-drop.net.
Preserve and analyze KB5034441_update.exe, including its hash, signature, origin, and any network or persistence activity.
